description.short_caption: Portable chest radiograph showing bilateral lung findings.
description.detailed_description: This is a portable chest radiograph taken in a sitting position. The image shows bilateral lung fields with diffuse opacities, particularly in the lower zones, which may indicate consolidation or effusion. The heart appears enlarged, and there is obscuration of the diaphragmatic contours, suggesting possible pleural effusion. The mediastinum is midline, and no obvious pneumothorax is visible.
visible_findings: bilateral diffuse opacities in lung fields

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the chest showing bilateral pulmonary findings.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral lung fields with areas of ground-glass opacities and consolidation, particularly in the lower lobes. The heart and mediastinal structures are centrally located, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The findings suggest an infectious or inflammatory process in the lungs.

Case_08018/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Wet mount of tracheal aspirate sputum specimen (also see Video 1).

description.short_caption: Wet mount of tracheal aspirate showing coiled larvae amidst cellular debris.
description.detailed_description: This wet mount image shows a microscopic view of a tracheal aspirate specimen. The central focus is on coiled larvae, likely parasitic, surrounded by numerous round cells and debris. The background appears granular, consistent with cellular material and mucus. The image suggests the presence of a parasitic infection, with the larvae being a key diagnostic finding.

description.short_caption: Wet mount of tracheal aspirate showing motile helminths.
description.detailed_description: This wet mount image of a tracheal aspirate reveals several elongated, coiled structures consistent with motile helminths. The background contains cellular debris and particulate matter. The helminths are prominent and appear to have a smooth, translucent surface. The image likely represents a parasitic infection involving the respiratory tract.

Case_08018/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Culture of sputum specimen, with serpiginous tracts.

description.short_caption: Culture plate showing growth with serpiginous tracts from a sputum specimen.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a culture plate with a red agar medium, likely blood agar. Multiple white, fuzzy colonies are visible, with serpiginous (snake-like) tracts radiating outward from some colonies. Two antibiotic discs labeled 'P' and 'A' are present, suggesting susceptibility testing. The colonies and tracts are consistent with fungal or filamentous bacterial growth, potentially indicative of an infectious process.
